## Change (Q4: A, first-come, first-served ticket queue; Q5: A, separate PR)

- **Concurrency.** Each run gets its own group (`workflow-failure-heal-intake-run-<id>`, `workflow-failure-heal-recovery-scan-<id>`). `HEAL_INTAKE_QUEUE_ENABLED=false` brings back the shared group (rollback).
- **`scripts/workflow_failure_heal_queue.sh`.**

    1. finds the lowest-numbered open `ai:heal-intake-queue` issue written by the GH_PAT login, and opens one if none is open (if two runs open one at once, the loser closes its own);

    3. polls every 20 s until no older live ticket remains.
  - `release` (`if: always()`) deletes the ticket.

2026-10-23T06:31:41.9181679Z   pr_body: ## Problem

`.github/workflows/workflow-failure-heal-intake.yml` puts every report in one concurrency group (`workflow-failure-heal-intake`, `cancel-in-progress: false`). GitHub keeps one running and one pending run per group, and it cancels the pending run when a newer one is queued. In a burst, every report but the first and the last was cancelled before any job read it. Nothing is logged, and GitHub keeps no payload for a cancelled run.

- About 15 `repository_dispatch` intake runs ended `cancelled` with no jobs at all.

2026-10-23T06:31:22.6177574Z   pr_body: ## Problem

`.github/workflows/workflow-failure-heal-intake.yml` puts every report in one concurrency group (`workflow-failure-heal-intake`, `cancel-in-progress: false`). GitHub keeps one running and one pending run per group, and it cancels the pending run when a newer one is queued. In a burst, every report but the first and the last was cancelled before any job read it. Nothing is logged, and GitHub keeps no payload for a cancelled run.

Evidence from 2026-10-21:
- About 15 `repository_dispatch` intake runs ended `cancelled` with no jobs at all.
- One burst at 16:11:13–16:12:18 UTC: four reports arrived. 39632513629 and 39632666372 were cancelled; 39632505050 and 39632667113 ran. The two that ran were AI Validate `engine_fallback` reports with different fingerprints.

## Change (Q4: A, first-come, first-served ticket queue; Q5: A, separate PR)

- **Concurrency.** Each run gets its own group (`workflow-failure-heal-intake-run-<id>`, `workflow-failure-heal-recovery-scan-<id>`). `HEAL_INTAKE_QUEUE_ENABLED=false` brings back the shared group (rollback).
- **`scripts/workflow_failure_heal_queue.sh`.**
  - `acquire` runs in both jobs from the trusted checkout, before engine setup:
    1. finds the lowest-numbered open `ai:heal-intake-queue` issue written by the GH_PAT login, and opens one if none is open (if two runs open one at once, the loser closes its own);
    2. posts a ticket (`<!-- ai:heal-intake-queue:v1 run= attempt= job= -->` as the last line);
    3. polls every 20 s until no older live ticket remains.
  - `release` (`if: always()`) deletes the ticket.

`codex_isolated_exec.sh prepare --deps` installed only the repository root's `package.json`. In tele-funtoken-msg-scoring the root has none, so implement run 39832670917 logged `stage-deps node=none python=requirements`. The review sandbox (`scripts/review_untrusted_sandbox.sh` → `scripts/review_untrusted_workspace.py`) leaves every `dist`, `build` and `coverage` directory out of its copy of the repository, including committed ones. - `snapshot` records the committed build-output directories it hid, names and file counts only, in `<manifest>.hidden_build_dirs.json`. It logs only a count (`REVIEW_ISOLATION_SNAPSHOT hidden_build_dirs=<n>`).
- A new `hidden-note MANIFEST` subcommand turns that list into a short "Directories left out of this sandbox copy" note: at most 40 entries, plain-ASCII paths only, skipping anything under dot directories, `node_modules` or secret-like names.
- `review_untrusted_sandbox.sh run` appends the note to the prompt after installing it, for both the Claude and the OpenCode paths. It is advisory and fail-open.

Nothing new enters the sandbox copy or write-back, so the security model is unchanged.
